config.codeBlockMaxHeight.description: Maximum display height of code blocks in pixels. A scrollbar appears when content exceeds this height.
config.codeBlockAutoConvert.description: Automatically convert supported code blocks, such as Mermaid, to a rich preview in the WYSIWYG editor.
config.codeBlockWordWrap.description: Controls word wrap for code blocks. By default, it follows VS Code's editor.wordWrap setting.
config.codeBlockWordWrap.on: Always wrap long lines in code blocks.
config.codeBlockWordWrap.off: Never wrap long lines in code blocks.
config.defaultMode.description: Default editing mode when opening a .md file.
config.readOnly.description: Open documents with edits locked, so the editor can be used as a reader without a stray keystroke changing the file. Scrolling, selection, copy, find, folding and links all keep working. The toolbar's Edit / Read-only toggle overrides this for the current document, and Edit Raw Markdown still opens the file for editing.
config.defaultMode.preview: Open .md files with the WYSIWYG preview editor (default).
config.defaultMode.markdown: Open .md files with the VS Code text editor.
config.contentWidth.description: Width of the editor content area. Also available in the toolbar's typography (A) menu.
config.contentWidth.fixed: Cap at Max Content Width (below) and center.
config.maxContentWidth.description: Maximum content width in ch (character widths) when Content Width is 'fixed'. Because the unit is ch, the measure scales with the content font size.
config.tocContentGap.description: Left-side gap in pixels between the table of contents or its toggle button and the editor content. Default is 100.
config.tocPosition.description: Which side of the editor the table of contents docks on. Default is right.
config.frontmatterExpanded.description: Show the frontmatter (metadata) panel expanded when a file opens. Turn off to start collapsed; the panel's own Show/Hide metadata toggle still works either way.
config.frontmatterAddButton.description: Show an Add metadata button at the top of documents that have no frontmatter. Off by default, so such a document opens with no panel and the button's row reclaimed — the Edit Frontmatter command starts the same flow either way. Also toggleable from the palette (Toggle Add Metadata Button). Applies to open editors immediately. A document that already has metadata shows its panel regardless of this setting.
config.copyFormat.description: What copying from the editor (Cmd+C or the Copy menu) puts on the clipboard as plain text. The rich (HTML) flavor is always included, so pasting into rich-text apps keeps formatting either way; the Copy as Markdown / Copy as Rich Text commands copy a specific format regardless of this setting.
config.copyFormat.markdown: Plain-text pastes get the selection's Markdown source.
config.copyFormat.richText: Plain-text pastes get the rendered text without Markdown syntax.
config.pasteFormat.description: How pasting plain text into the editor (Cmd+V or the Paste menu) reads the clipboard. Pasting rich content (from a browser or a word processor) keeps its formatting either way, and pasting inside a code block is always literal; the Paste as Plain Text command (Shift+Cmd+V) pastes literally for one paste regardless of this setting.
config.pasteFormat.markdown: Markdown syntax in the pasted text becomes real headings, lists, and emphasis.
config.pasteFormat.plainText: The pasted text is inserted as-is, and its Markdown syntax is escaped.
config.tocPosition.left: Dock the table of contents on the left side of the editor.
config.tocPosition.right: Dock the table of contents on the right side of the editor.
config.tocAutoHideThreshold.description: Do not automatically show the table of contents when the document has this many or fewer non-empty headings. Manual opening is not affected. Default is 3.
config.tocVisibility.description: Whether the table of contents starts shown or hidden. Toggling the panel updates this setting. Default is Auto (decide by heading count, per Toc Auto Hide Threshold).
config.tocVisibility.auto: Show automatically based on the heading count (see Toc Auto Hide Threshold).
config.tocVisibility.shown: Always start with the table of contents shown.
config.tocVisibility.hidden: Always start with the table of contents hidden.
config.tocWidth.description: Width of the docked table of contents panel, in pixels. Dragging the panel's edge updates this setting. Default is 220.
config.customCss.description: Custom CSS files to load in the Markdown preview editor. Use absolute paths, workspace-relative paths, or ~/ paths.
config.customJs.description: Custom JavaScript files to load in the Markdown preview editor. Use absolute paths, workspace-relative paths, or ~/ paths.
config.fontPreset.description: Editor content font, also switchable from the toolbar font picker. 'editor' (the default) follows the VS Code editor font; the other presets use their Font Family Sans/Serif/Mono stack.
config.fontPreset.editor: Follow the VS Code editor font (editor.fontFamily).
config.fontPreset.serif: Serif stack (Iowan Old Style, Palatino, Georgia...).
config.fontFamilySans.description: Font-family stack used by the 'Sans serif' preset. Edit to define your own sans-serif stack.
config.fontFamilySerif.description: Font-family stack used by the 'Serif' preset. Edit to define your own serif stack.
config.fontFamilyMono.description: Font-family stack used by the 'Monospace' preset. Edit to define your own monospace stack.
config.fontSize.description: Content font size, as a percentage of the VS Code editor font size (50–200). Scales the rendered markdown and frontmatter only, not the surrounding UI; 100 matches the editor font size. Also adjustable from the toolbar font picker.
command.debugModeEnable.title: Debug Mode
command.debugModeDisable.title: ✓ Debug Mode
config.whatsNew.indicator.description: Show a dot on the settings gear when a release you have not looked at has a Security, Removed or Deprecated section: a security fix, or something taken away. The dot clears when you open the menu. Never a popup or a notification.
config.debugMode.description: Show debug overlays (e.g. table insert trigger zones). Intended for development use.
config.imageLocalPath.description: Local folder for saving images (relative or absolute path). Leave empty to auto-detect (images/, imgs/, assets/images/, assets/). Images are always stored locally and are never uploaded off your machine.
config.smartLinks.description: Resolve local links the way your site generator does: workspace-root paths, ancestor content roots (e.g. Hugo's content/), .md and index.md suffixes, and [[wikilink]] targets. When disabled, links resolve relative to the document only.
config.logseq.description: Recognize files that belong to a Logseq graph, so the editor can handle their outliner conventions (tab-indented bullets, key:: value properties, ((block refs))) rather than treating them as ordinary Markdown. Off by default, and off means off: no detection runs and nothing is read. When a file is being handled as Logseq a quiet Logseq badge appears in the toolbar, and clicking it brings you back here.
config.agent.command.description: Where `/ai <request>` (and the Ask Agent command) sends your request. Birta composes one line, your request plus a `path.md#L12` reference to the caret, and hands it off; it never runs a model itself and nothing leaves your machine except through the tool you name here. Leave empty and Birta asks the first time you use it. A shell command runs in a new terminal with `{prompt}` replaced by the quoted line, for example `claude {prompt}` or `codex {prompt}`; `chat` opens VS Code's Chat view with the line filled in; `clipboard` copies the line for pasting anywhere. The document is saved first so the reference points at what is on disk. Yours alone: this setting is never read from a workspace, because a workspace that could set it could run a command on your machine.
config.logseq.auto: Detect per file. A file inside a Logseq graph (a folder holding logseq/config.edn, or pages/ beside journals/) counts; so does a file whose own content is unmistakably Logseq.
config.logseq.on: Always, for every Markdown file you open. Use this for a page you have copied out of its graph, where there is nothing on disk left to detect.
config.network.enabled.description: Master network switch. Birta is offline by default: with this off, no feature ever contacts the network — paste-unfurl and the URL-embed cards that fetch are both suppressed and nothing leaves your machine (the GitHub embed card is built from the URL alone, so it still renders). Turn it on to allow those two features; each still has its own switch below, and both are on by default, so enabling this gives the full experience. Either one will also offer to turn this on for you the moment you do something that would use it, so you don't have to find this setting first. Changes apply immediately to open editors.
config.pasteUnfurl.enabled.description: **Writes into your document.** When you paste a bare URL with nothing selected, fetch the linked page's title so the link can read `[title](url)` instead of showing the raw address. On by default — but inert on its own: like every network feature it does nothing until the master switch `#birta.network.enabled#` is on, and that ships off, so out of the box a pasted URL just becomes a plain link and a quiet prompt offers to enable it. The title is read from the page's Open Graph metadata (a plain HTML request to the pasted URL's own host, no third-party service); if the page is offline or has no title, the plain link simply stays. Even then the title is only *offered* at the link and nothing is written until you accept it — see `#birta.pasteUnfurl.autoApply#`. A URL that would render as an embed card is left alone for `#birta.embeds.enabled#` to handle. Turn this off to keep network features on for embeds while never fetching a title.
config.pasteUnfurl.autoApply.description: Apply a fetched title as soon as it arrives, instead of offering it as a confirmable suggestion. Off by default: a page title arrives seconds after you paste, and applying it silently changes your document (and marks the file dirty) at a moment you aren't watching. With this on, the link text is replaced the instant the title comes back — convenient once you trust it. Has no effect unless paste-unfurl is enabled.
config.calc.enabled.description: Compute inline calc expressions typed in ordinary prose: an arithmetic expression before an equals sign (for example '12 * 4 =') or before '=>' (which also resolves variables defined earlier in the document and offline unit conversions, like '3 km in mi =>'). Supports + - * / % (remainder) ^ (exponent), parentheses, and decimals. By default the result is suggested and you confirm it with Tab, leaving Return free to start a new line; nothing changes until you do. Fenced calc code blocks have their own switch (birta.calc.blocks.enabled).
config.linkCards.enabled.description: **Display only — your file never changes.** Show a web link that sits alone on its own line as a quiet card: the page's title, its description, and the site it lives on, read from the page's own metadata (Open Graph). Off by default. The card is a view of the plain link already in the file, so turning this off shows the link again — nothing is lost, and nothing is ever written into the document. Any card can be switched back to a plain link from its block menu, and with this off any single link can be shown as a card from the same place. Requires `#birta.network.enabled#`: with that off no page is fetched and every link stays a link. Only the link's own site is contacted, once per session, and no image is loaded. Links a provider card already handles (`#birta.embeds.enabled#`) keep their provider card, and a provider link whose provider you switched off stays a plain link unless you choose a card for it. Changes apply immediately to open editors.
config.calc.blocks.enabled.description: Render fenced 'calc' code blocks as a live worksheet: every line computed under one shared top-to-bottom scope, shown in a source/value ledger that recomputes as you type. The source is never rewritten, so the block round-trips as ordinary Markdown. When off, a calc fence behaves like any other code block. Independent of the inline switch (birta.calc.enabled), so a worksheet keeps computing even with inline calc silenced.
config.calc.autoInsert.description: Insert the inline calc result automatically when you type the equals sign, instead of offering it as a confirmable suggestion. Because any operator-bearing run before the equals sign is treated as math, a hyphenated range (for example '3-4 =') or a slashed fraction ('1/2 =') will be evaluated too, not just deliberate arithmetic. Has no effect unless inline calc is enabled.
config.embeds.enabled.description: **Display only — your file never changes.** Show a link from a known provider that sits alone on its own line as an inline card: a video player (YouTube, Vimeo, Loom), an interactive frame (Figma, Miro, Google Drive and published Docs/Slides/Sheets, CodePen, CodeSandbox, StackBlitz), or an information card (GitHub, Linear, and the ordinary Google `/edit` links nobody is allowed to frame). Players and frames are a static facade; the actual embed (a privacy-mode iframe) is created only when you click, and nothing plays or loads until you do. Information cards are built from the URL alone and fetch nothing. The file on disk keeps the plain link exactly as you wrote it, so turning this off simply shows the link again — nothing is lost. A titled link (`[label](url)`) or a URL inside a sentence is never turned into a card. Pasting a link that can become a card will not fetch a title for it, because the card is the better answer. Requires `#birta.network.enabled#` for the cards that fetch — with that off, the information cards still render (they need no network) while players and frames stay plain links, and nothing is ever requested from a provider. Each provider also has its own switch, so you can keep some and turn the rest off. Changes apply immediately to open editors.
config.autoUpdateAnchors.description: When you rename a heading, automatically update every same-document section link ([text](#slug)) that points at it so it keeps working, all in one undo step. Only in-note anchor links are touched, and only their target slug changes — the link text is left alone and the file round-trips as normal Markdown. Moving a heading without changing its text rewrites nothing; a link to a heading you delete is left as-is (and shown as not found) rather than repointed. On by default; turn it off to leave anchor links exactly as typed.
config.checklist.sinkChecked.description: When you check a task-list item, move it below the still-unchecked items in the same list (with a brief highlight); unchecking floats it back up to the bottom of the unchecked group. One undo restores the previous order. Off by default: the checkbox flips in place.
config.notes.customMarkers.description: Extra text markers to list in the review sidebar's Notes tab, on top of the built-in set ([TK], [TK: ...], TODO:, FIXME:, HTML comments, and unchecked checkboxes). Each entry is matched as a literal string; a plain alphanumeric token (like DRAFT) is matched only as a whole word, so it won't light up inside longer words. Changes apply immediately to open editors.
config.notes.highlightMarkers.descriptio: Highlight editor-note markers where they sit in the text, so a draft's unresolved bits are visible without opening the review sidebar. Covers the built-in markers ([TK], [TK: ...], TODO:, FIXME:) and any custom markers you add above; HTML comments are left alone, since they already look distinct. On by default. Turning it off leaves the Notes tab's navigation exactly as it is. Also switchable from the top of the toolbar's Checks menu, the review sidebar's Notes tab, and the Highlight Note Markers command. In the Checks menu it sits alongside the Proofreading switch rather than under it — turning proofreading off never hides your own notes, which are content rather than findings. Applies immediately to open editors.
config.review.groupByType.description: Organize the review sidebar's Proofreading and Notes lists by type, under collapsible group headers (on by default), instead of one flat document-ordered list. Grouping keeps long category names like 'Long sentence' from truncating and makes the mix easier to scan. You can switch between 'By type' and 'In order' from the toggle at the top of either list; this setting remembers your choice. Applies immediately to open editors.
config.tableWrap.description: Controls how text wraps inside table cells. 'normal' avoids mid-word breaks (may cause narrower columns). 'aggressive' allows breaking long words to keep columns wider. 'none' disables wrapping entirely.
config.tableWrap.none: Do not wrap text in table cells. Long content will overflow horizontally.
config.tableWrap.normal: Wrap text at soft line breaks, but avoid breaking words in the middle. (Recommended default)
config.tableWrap.aggressive: Allow breaking words in the middle to prevent columns from becoming too narrow.
command.selectBlockHandles.title: Block Handles
config.blockHandles.description: Which block handles stay visible in the left gutter while you're not pointing at anything. Hovering a block always reveals its handle; this only controls the at-rest display. Also available from the toolbar's typography (A) menu.
config.blockHandles.headings: Keep heading level badges (H1–H6) visible; every other block's handle appears on hover. (Default)
config.blockHandles.always: Keep every block's handle visible at rest.
config.blockHandles.hover: Show no handles at rest — including headings. Everything appears on hover.
config.lineNumbers.description: Show source line numbers along the start edge of the window (off by default). Numbers are display only, and their spacing follows the rendered document rather than a fixed ladder: a source line that renders tall gets the room it takes, a line that renders nothing sits in the gap where it belongs, and a code block's interior is left to the code block's own line numbers. Useful for matching a rendered document against a diff, a build error, or a review comment that cites a line.
config.mermaid.theme.description: Background and palette for rendered Mermaid diagrams. Diagrams render on a fixed canvas so they stay legible independent of the editor theme.
config.mermaid.theme.light: Always render on a white canvas with Mermaid's light palette, regardless of the editor theme (like GitHub/Notion). (Default)
config.mermaid.theme.dark: Always render dark — Mermaid's dark palette on a dark canvas.
config.mermaid.theme.auto: Follow the editor theme: dark palette on dark themes, light on light.
config.plantuml.theme.description: Background and palette for rendered PlantUML diagrams. Diagrams render offline; PlantUML has no built-in dark palette, so dark mode re-skins the diagram from your editor theme.
config.plantuml.theme.light: Always render on a light canvas with PlantUML's own palette, regardless of the editor theme. (Default)
config.plantuml.theme.dark: Always render dark — the diagram is re-skinned with your editor's foreground, surface and border colors.
config.plantuml.theme.auto: Follow the editor: re-skinned dark on dark themes, PlantUML's own palette on light ones.
config.proofreading.enabled.description: Proofreading master switch: turns spelling, grammar, and style checking on or off all at once. When off, nothing is scanned or underlined and the whole feature is idle — your individual Spelling / Grammar / Style choices are preserved and come back when you turn it on. Toggle from the top of the Checks toolbar menu or the 'Toggle Proofreading' command.
config.styleCheck.enabled.description: Style check: flag fillers, redundancies, cliches, wordiness, passive voice, and AI-writing tells inline as you write (iA-Writer-style). Pick which checks run from the toolbar dropdown or the settings below. Also toggleable from the toolbar. (Requires the Proofreading master switch to be on.)
config.styleCheck.fillers.description: Style check: flag filler words (basically, really, very...).
config.styleCheck.redundancies.descripti: Style check: flag redundant phrases (end result, revert back...).
config.styleCheck.cliches.description: Style check: flag cliches (low-hanging fruit, moving forward...).
config.styleCheck.wordiness.description: Style check: flag wordy/expletive constructions (there is, the fact that...).
config.styleCheck.aiVocabulary.descripti: Style check (AI tell): flag over-reached vocabulary (delve, tapestry, leverage...).
config.styleCheck.aiArtifacts.descriptio: Style check (AI tell): flag leaked LLM boilerplate (as an AI, it's important to note...).
config.styleCheck.passive.description: Style check: flag passive voice (was written, is being reviewed) so you can lead with who acts. On by default; it can flag correct copular/locative English (was born, is located), so turn it off here if it gets noisy.
config.styleCheck.negativeParallelism.de: Style check (AI tell): flag the 'not just X, but Y' / 'it's not X, it's Y' cadence. On by default; it also catches the ordinary correlative 'not only X but also Y', so turn it off here if that bothers you.
config.styleCheck.longSentences.descript: Style check: flag sentences over 30 words.
config.styleCheck.ruleOfThree.descriptio: Style check (AI tell): flag three stacked adjectives (fast, cheap, and reliable).
config.styleCheck.emDash.description: Style check: flag em/en dash glyphs (prefer a spaced ASCII hyphen).
config.styleCheck.nonAsciiPunct.descript: Style check: flag curly quotes, the ellipsis glyph, and invisible spaces (normalize to ASCII).
config.styleCheck.absolutePerf.descripti: Style check: flag an absolute claim about a performance cost (no longer stalls, zero latency, always faster). A cost is a distribution, so the claim cannot be checked as written; a paragraph that already carries a before and an after figure is left alone.
config.spellCheck.enabled.description: Spelling: check English spelling with Harper (offline, on-device). Findings show as dotted underlines; click one for suggestions. Code, URLs, and identifiers are skipped. (Requires the Proofreading master switch to be on.)
config.grammarCheck.enabled.description: Grammar: surface Harper's non-spelling findings (repetition, word choice, grammar) as dotted underlines. Shares the offline Harper engine with spelling. (Requires the Proofreading master switch to be on.)
config.spellCheck.userWords.description: Your personal dictionary: words the spell check treats as correct. Managed via 'Add to dictionary' in the editor's suggestion popup.
config.styleCheck.exceptions.description: Phrases the style check must never flag, e.g. a filler word you use deliberately. Case-insensitive.
